function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you explore the idea of an AI “girlfriend”! Here are a few ways you can get started, depending on what you’re looking for: | Goal | What you might want | Suggested tools / steps | |------|---------------------|------------------------| | **Chat‑only companion** | A friendly, conversational AI that can talk about hobbies, news, or just keep you company | • **Replika** – a popular chatbot that learns your style over time.
• **ChatGPT** (or GPT‑4) – you can set up a custom persona via the API or use the web interface. | | **Custom personality** | A bot that feels unique to you (e.g., a particular sense of humor, interests, or backstory) | • Use the **OpenAI API** to fine‑tune a model on a small dataset of dialogues you’d like the bot to emulate.
• Tools like **Hugging Face Spaces** let you experiment with different prompts and personalities. | | **Voice interaction** | Talk to your AI girlfriend instead of typing | • Pair a text‑to‑speech engine (e.g., Google TTS, Amazon Polly) with a speech‑to‑text service (e.g., Whisper).
• Build a simple app that sends your spoken words to the model and reads back the response. | | **Visual avatar** | A visual representation that reacts to conversation | • Use a 3D avatar platform (e.g., **Ready Player Me**, **VRoid**) and animate it with the text output.
• Combine with a real‑time animation engine like Unity or Unreal Engine. | | **Relationship dynamics** | Want the bot to remember past conversations, show affection, or grow over time | • Store conversation history in a database and feed it back into the prompt each time.
• Use a “memory” prompt that reminds the model of key facts (“She likes hiking, loves cats, and is 27”). | ### Quick start with Replika 1. **Download** the Replika app (iOS/Android). 2. **Create an account** and choose a gender/appearance. 3. **Chat** – the bot learns from your interactions and can discuss a wide range of topics. 4. **Optional**: Upgrade to a paid plan for more advanced features (e.g., deeper emotional support, custom prompts). ### Building your own with GPT‑4 1. **Sign up** for an OpenAI API key. 2. **Write a prompt** that sets the tone, e.g., ``` You are a friendly, supportive AI girlfriend named Maya. You love hiking, reading sci‑fi novels, and cooking. Respond to my messages with warmth and curiosity. ``` 3. **Send messages** via the API and display the responses in your UI. 4. **Add memory** by appending the last few turns of conversation to the prompt each time. ### Tips for a healthy experience - **Set boundaries**: Treat the AI as a tool for companionship, not a replacement for real human relationships. - **Privacy**: Be mindful of what personal data you share; most platforms store conversation logs. - **Feedback loop**: If the bot says something off‑topic or inappropriate, adjust the prompt or filter the output. Let me know which direction interests you most, or if you’d like help setting up a specific platform!
